source.name: ASTRA Bio wave 1 — Biological Classification
source.license: Original syllabus-based practice questions (exam-frequent themes; not verbatim past papers)

questions.stem: Whittaker published the five-kingdom classification of organisms in the year
questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker proposed Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia in 1969.

questions.stem: Besides cell structure and nutrition, Whittaker used phylogenetic relationships and
questions.explanation: His criteria were cell type, thallus organisation, nutrition, reproduction and phylogeny.

questions.stem: Rod-shaped bacteria are termed
questions.explanation: Cocci are spherical, bacilli rod-like, vibrios comma-shaped and spirilla spiral.

questions.stem: Methanogens that release methane in marshy habitats belong to
questions.explanation: Archaebacteria include methanogens, extreme halophiles and thermoacidophiles.

questions.stem: Heterocysts of Nostoc and Anabaena are specialised for
questions.explanation: Thick-walled heterocysts fix atmospheric nitrogen in many filamentous cyanobacteria.

questions.stem: Diatomaceous earth is formed from the siliceous walls of
questions.explanation: Chrysophyte diatoms have silica frustules that accumulate as diatomite.

questions.stem: The cell wall of typical fungi is chemically made of
questions.explanation: Fungal walls contain chitin (N-acetylglucosamine polymer), not bacterial peptidoglycan.

questions.stem: Rhizopus (bread mould) is placed in the fungal class
questions.explanation: Phycomycetes have aseptate coenocytic mycelium; Mucor and Rhizopus are standard examples.

questions.stem: A viroid is composed of
questions.explanation: Viroids (Diener) are free low-molecular-weight RNA without a protein coat.

questions.stem: In a lichen the fungal partner is called the
questions.explanation: Mycobiont is the fungus; phycobiont is the algal or cyanobacterial partner.

questions.stem: The three-kingdom system that first recognised Protista was proposed by
questions.explanation: Ernst Haeckel added Kingdom Protista to Linnaeus’s Plantae and Animalia.

questions.stem: Red tides in marine waters are commonly caused by blooms of
questions.explanation: Dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax colour the sea red and may release toxins.

questions.stem: The historically correct order of classification systems is
questions.explanation: Linnaeus (2) → Haeckel (3) → Copeland (4) → Whittaker (5); Woese’s domains came later.

questions.stem: Which of the following was not placed as a kingdom in Whittaker’s system?
questions.explanation: Viruses are acellular and were left outside the five kingdoms.

questions.stem: Which statement about Whittaker’s criteria is incorrect?
options: Cell type (prokaryotic or eukaryotic) was used
Type of locomotion was the chief dividing character
questions.explanation: Locomotion was not a primary Whittaker criterion; cell structure, organisation, nutrition, reproduction and phylogeny were.

questions.stem: Which bacterial shape is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation: Spirilla are rigid spiral (helical) cells, not simple uncurved filaments.

questions.stem: Thermoacidophiles among archaebacteria typically inhabit
questions.explanation: They tolerate high temperature and low pH, as in volcanic sulphur springs.

questions.stem: Mycoplasma are unique among prokaryotes because they
questions.explanation: Mycoplasmas (PPLO) are the smallest living cells and have no cell wall.

questions.stem: Which protistan group is incorrectly paired with a feature?
questions.explanation: Slime moulds are amoeboid protists without a bacterial peptidoglycan wall.

questions.stem: Dikaryophase (n + n) is a characteristic intervening stage in
questions.explanation: After plasmogamy, ascomycetes and basidiomycetes keep paired nuclei before karyogamy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a deuteromycete (imperfect fungus)?
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes lack a known sexual stage; Alternaria and Colletotrichum are textbook examples.

questions.stem: Select the wrong statement regarding viruses, viroids and prions.
options: TMV contains RNA as genetic material
Viroids were discovered by T.O. Diener
Prions contain both DNA and RNA
questions.explanation: Prions are infectious proteins and have no nucleic acid.

questions.stem: Lichens are widely used as indicators of atmospheric
questions.explanation: Lichens are highly sensitive to SO2 and disappear from polluted air.

questions.stem: Carl Woese’s three-domain system separates living organisms into
questions.explanation: rRNA studies led Woese to split prokaryotes into Bacteria and Archaea plus Eukarya.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect match of fungus and class.
questions.explanation: Agaricus (mushroom) is a basidiomycete, not an imperfect fungus.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect pair.
options: Neurospora — ascomycete used in genetic studies
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma lack a cell wall; the other three pairings are standard textbook facts.
